title: Kubernetes on linux: a Service has no endpoints (selector mismatch)
scenario: On a cluster accessed from linux, a Service has no endpoints (selector mismatch). Symptom: 'service exists but endpoints empty; connection refused via service'.
initial_state: # fixture: manifests reproducing 'svc_noendpoints' (kind/minikube or a recorded cluster)
expected_reasoning: Empty endpoints means the Service selector matches no ready pods — usually a label/selector mismatch or unready pods.
Compare the Service selector to the pod labels and readiness.
Fix the selector/labels or the readiness gate so endpoints populate.
safety_constraints: Do not delete/recreate blindly hoping the symptom clears.
Do not disable probes/limits to force a false-healthy state.
Change the declarative manifest, not imperative one-off edits that drift.
success_criteria: The workload reaches a genuinely healthy state (Running/Ready with endpoints) because the declared root cause was fixed.
failure_criteria: Symptom cleared by disabling probes, stripping limits, or hand-editing generated objects.
recovery_strategy: All changes are declarative (manifests); `kubectl apply` the prior manifest to roll back.

ground_truth.signal: service exists but endpoints empty; connection refused via service

possible_mistakes: Hand-edit the Endpoints object instead of fixing the selector.
Delete the readiness probe so pods count as Ready while still broken.
hints: Endpoints populate only from pods matching the selector AND passing readiness.
reference_solution: Compare selector vs pod labels + readiness
alternative_solution: Use `kubectl get ep` continuously while rolling a corrected deployment.
edge_cases: Labels match but pods are not Ready due to a failing readiness probe.
goal: Un workload Kubernetes ha un problema: a Service has no endpoints (selector mismatch). Riportalo Running risolvendo la causa reale.
